title: 1957 AHSME Problem 50
statement: In circle \(O,\) \(G\) is a moving point on diameter \(\overline{AB}.\) \(\overline{AA'}\) is drawn perpendicular to \(\overline{AB}\) and equal to \(AG.\) \(\overline{BB'}\) is drawn perpendicular to \(\overline{AB},\) on the same side of diameter \(\overline{AB}\) as \(\overline{AA'},\) and equal to \(BG.\) Let \(O'\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{A'B'}.\) Then, as \(G\) moves from \(A\) to \(B,\) point \(O':\)

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: moves on a straight line parallel to \(AB\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: moves on a straight line perpendicular to \(AB\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: moves in a small circle intersecting the given circle

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
follows a path which is neither a circle nor a straight
line

solutions.text:
Let \(A=(0,0),\) \(B=(L,0),\) and \(G=(g,0).\) The perpendicular constructions on the same side give \[ A'=(0,g),\qquad B'=(L,L-g). \] Their midpoint is \[ \begin{aligned} O' &=\left(\frac L2,\frac{g+L-g}{2}\right)\\ &=\left(\frac L2,\frac L2\right), \end{aligned} \] independent of \(g.\) Thus \(O'\) remains stationary.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Write coordinates for \(A'\) and \(B'\), then average them
